description.value: The Revelstoke Visual Arts Centre is a non-profit public art gallery and community centre housed in Revelstoke's former police station, lending it a distinctive historical character complete with original jail cells visitors are invited to explore. The gallery presents rotating solo and group shows across one main open space and three adjoining side galleries, while the broader facility includes a community woodshop, pottery studio, xeriscape gardens, and outdoor picnic seating. It is one of the first buildings visible when arriving in Revelstoke off Highway 1, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists riding into town.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, active public attraction centrally located on the Highway 1 corridor into Revelstoke, with public washrooms confirmed — a useful waypoint for touring cyclists exploring town.
enrichment_extras.notes: Admission to the public gallery is by suggested donation ($5); the website notes visitors who cannot donate are still welcome. The pottery studio and woodshop are accessible 24/7 to members with a key fob.

wow_evidence: Non-profit gallery in the former police station, original jail cells open to explore — characterful setting lifts an ordinary gallery.
blurb: Public art gallery in Revelstoke's old police station; the original jail cells are part of the visit.
